extracted.intended_audience: graduate students (or advanced undergraduates) studying functional analysis/partial differential equations
extracted.subtask_description: A sequence of graduate-level problems and exercises (with hints) in functional analysis and Sobolev spaces, asking to prove structural theorems (extreme points, subdifferentials, Ekeland principle, operator adjoints, weak topologies, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extreme point equivalence (Problem 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that a ∈ K is an extreme point iff the set K\{a} is convex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness in convex decomposition (Problem 1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a be an extreme point of K. Let (xi)1≤i≤n be a finite sequence in K and let (αi)1≤i≤n be a finite sequence of real numbers such that αi>0 ∀i, ∑αi =1, and ∑αixi = a. Prove that xi = a ∀i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Singleton extreme set equivalence (Problem 1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that a is an extreme point iff {a} is an extreme set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximizer set is extreme (Problem 1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A ⊂ K be an extreme set and let f ∈ E*. Set B = {x ∈ A; ⟨f, x⟩ = max_{y∈A} ⟨f, y⟩}. Prove that B is an extreme subset of K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal element existence in extreme subsets (Problem 1.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M ⊂ K be an extreme set of K. Consider the collection F of all extreme sets of K contained in M with ordering A ≤ B iff B ⊂ A. Prove that F has a maximal element M0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal extreme set is a point (Problem 1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that the maximal element M0 (from previous question) is reduced to a single point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use Hahn–Banach and question 4.]

rubrics_metrics.name: K equals closed convex hull of extreme points (Problem 1.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that K coincides with the closed convex hull of all its extreme points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Argue by contradiction and use Hahn–Banach.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify extreme points of unit ball in examples (Problem 1.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the set E of all extreme points of B_E (the closed unit ball) in the following cases: (a) E = ℓ^∞, (b) E = c, (c) E = c0, (d) E = ℓ^1, (e) E = ℓ^p with 1<p<∞, (f) E = L^1(ℝ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [For the notation see Section 11.3].

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdifferential closed convexity (Problem 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that ∂ϕ(x) is a closed convex subset of E* for a convex function ϕ : E → (−∞, +∞] (ϕ ≠ +∞).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotonicity of subdifferential differences (Problem 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let x1, x2 ∈ D(∂ϕ), f1 ∈ ∂ϕ(x1), and f2 ∈ ∂ϕ(x2). Prove that ⟨f1 − f2, x1 − x2⟩ ≥ 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgradient duality identity (Problem 2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that f ∈ ∂ϕ(x) ⇔ ϕ(x) + ϕ*(f) = ⟨f, x⟩ (where ϕ* denotes the convex conjugate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute subdifferentials in examples (Problem 2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine ∂ϕ in the following cases: (a) ϕ(x)=1/2||x||^2, (b) ϕ(x)=||x||, (c) ϕ=I_K the indicator of a convex set K (resp. linear subspace), (d) ϕ differentiable convex function on E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: In cases (a),(b) relate ∂ϕ to the duality map F; see Exercise 1.1.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum of subdifferentials inclusion (Problem 2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ψ : E → (−∞,+∞] be another convex function (ψ≠+∞). Assume D(ϕ) ∩ D(ψ) ≠ ∅. Prove ∂ϕ(x) + ∂ψ(x) ⊂ ∂(ϕ + ψ)(x) ∀x ∈ E and construct an example where inclusion is strict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Convention: A + B = ∅ if either set empty.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonemptiness of subdifferential under local boundedness (Problem 2.B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under assumption ∃M∈ℝ, ∃R>0 s.t. ϕ(x) ≤ M ∀x with ||x−x0|| ≤ R, prove ∂ϕ(x0) ≠ ∅.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use Hahn–Banach in E × ℝ.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Bound on subgradient norms (Problem 2.B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the same local boundedness assumption prove a uniform bound on ||f|| for f ∈ ∂ϕ(x0) (explicit inequality given in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Lipschitz property from bounded subgradients (Problem 2.B3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that for all r<R there exists L≥0 such that |ϕ(x1) − ϕ(x2)| ≤ L||x1 − x2|| for x1,x2 with ||xi − x0|| ≤ r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [See also Exercise 2.1 for alternative proof.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior of domain equality (Problem 2.B4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E Banach and ϕ l.s.c., prove Int D(∂ϕ) = Int D(ϕ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Directional derivative via subdifferential (Problem 2.B5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that for every y ∈ E, lim_{t↓0} (ϕ(x0 + ty) − ϕ(x0))/t = max_{f∈∂ϕ(x0)} ⟨f,y⟩.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Look at Exercise 1.25, question 5.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact sum rule for subdifferentials under domain condition (Problem 2.B6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let ψ convex with x0 ∈ D(ψ). Prove ∂ϕ(x) + ∂ψ(x) = ∂(ϕ + ψ)(x) ∀x ∈ E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Given f0 ∈ ∂(ϕ + ψ)(x), apply Theorem 1.12 to functions φ(y)=ϕ(y)−ϕ(x)−⟨f0,y−x⟩ and ψ̃(y)=ψ(y)−ψ(x).]

rubrics_metrics.name: ε-subdifferential density property (Problem 3.B main statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given Banach E and convex l.s.c. ϕ≠+∞, for ε>0 and x∈D(ϕ) define ∂_εϕ(x). Show that for any x0 ∈ D(ϕ) and f0 ∈ ∂_εϕ(x0) and any λ>0 there exists x1 ∈ D(ϕ) and f1 ∈ ∂ϕ(x1) with ||x1 − x0|| ≤ ε/λ and ||f1 − f0|| ≤ λ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to solve Problem 2 before this one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ekeland variational principle construction (Problem 3.A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given complete metric space (M,d) and l.s.c. ψ bounded below, prove existence of a∈M s.t. ψ(x) − ψ(a) + d(x,a) ≥ 0 ∀x ∈ M by constructing nested S(x) sets and a Cauchy sequence (xn) via choices using εn→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: 1) define S(x)={y; ψ(y) − ψ(x) + d(x,y) ≤ 0}; 2) inductively choose xn+1∈S(xn) with near-infimum property; 3) show Cauchy; 4) conclude. Geometric interpretation requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Ekeland to obtain ε-subdifferential approximations (Problem 3.B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider ψ(x)=ϕ(x)+ϕ*(f0)−⟨f0,x⟩. Prove existence of x1 with ||x1−x0|| ≤ ε/λ and ψ(x)−ψ(x1)+λ||x−x1|| ≥0 ∀x, using part A and an appropriate closed set M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclude existence of exact subgradient (Problem 3.B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: From previous step and Problem 2, deduce existence of f1 ∈ ∂ϕ(x1) with required bounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use result of Problem 2, question B6.]

rubrics_metrics.name: D(∂ϕ) and range equalities (Problem 3.B3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce D(∂ϕ) = D(ϕ) and R(∂ϕ) = D(ϕ*) (where R(∂ϕ) = {f ∈ E*; ∃x∈D(∂ϕ) with f∈∂ϕ(x)}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of norm-attaining functionals for bounded convex sets (Problem 3.C1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let C⊂E closed convex bounded. Prove { f∈E*; sup_{x∈C} ⟨f,x⟩ is achieved } is dense in E*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Apply part B to ϕ = I_C.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting hyperplanes are dense on boundary (Problem 3.C2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove set of points in C that admit a supporting hyperplane is dense in boundary(C) (C closed convex bounded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asplund iterative construction (Problem 4.A1–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two convex functions ϕ0,ψ0≥0 with ϕ0(0)=ψ0(0)=0 define inductively ϕ_{n+1}=(ϕn+ψn)/2 and ψ_{n+1}=(1/2){ϕn(x+y)+ψn(x−y)}. Check 0≤ψn≤ϕn, convexity, monotonicity (ϕn nonincreasing, ψn nondecreasing), and existence of common convex limit θ with ψ0 ≤ θ ≤ ϕ0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity and conjugate identity in iterative scheme (Problem 4.A4–6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish continuity properties (ϕn,ψn continuous at x0 if ϕ0 continuous at x0), and show conjugate formula ϕ_{n+1}^*(f) = (1/2) inf_{g} {ϕ_n^*(f+g) + ψ_n^*(f−g)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Apply question 2 of Exercise 2.1.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratic-homogeneous convex function inequalities (Problem 4.B)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ homogeneous of order two, prove convexity/ seminorm properties and inequalities: ϕ(x + y) ≤ (1/t) ϕ(x) + (1/(1−t)) ϕ(y) etc., and derive inequality (1) 4ϕ(x) ≤ (1/t)ϕ(x+y) + (1/(1−t))ϕ(x−y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use homogeneity to show seminorm structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control relation between iterates under homogeneity (Problem 4.B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ0,ψ0 homogeneous of order two and ϕ0 ≤ (1+C)ψ0, prove for all n: ϕn(x) ≤ (1 + C/4^n) ψn(x) ∀x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Induction and use inequality (1).]

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict convexity preservation (Problem 4.B3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming either ϕ0 or ψ0 strictly convex, prove the common limit θ is strictly convex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: use inequality in B2 and decomposition ϕn = θn + 2^{-n}ϕ0.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct strictly convex equivalent norm with strictly convex dual (Problem 4.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two equivalent norms ||·||_1 and ||·||_2 with strictly convex dual norms, prove existence of a third equivalent norm which is strictly convex and whose dual is strictly convex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use previous regularization/iteration results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive linear functionals: closedness of F (Problem 5.A1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let P convex cone in n.v.s. E, F = P − P. Assuming (i) every linear functional nonnegative on P is continuous, prove F is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Given x0∉F, construct a linear functional f with f(x0)=1 and f=0 on F.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite dimensional bound on complement subspaces (Problem 5.A2)
rubrics_metrics.description: With (i) as above, show any linear subspace M with M ∩ F = {0} has finite dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use Exercise 1.5.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclude (i)⇒(ii) for cones (Problem 5.A3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce that (i) ⇒ (ii): F is closed of finite codimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition with bounded pieces when P−P=E (Problem 5.B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume E Banach and P closed and P−P=E. Prove ∃C>0 s.t. every x∈E decomposes x=y−z with y,z∈P and ||y||,||z|| ≤ C||x||.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Consider set K={x=y−z; y,z∈P, ||y||≤1,||z||≤1} and use open mapping theorem idea.]

rubrics_metrics.name: From decomposition to continuity of positive functionals (Problem 5.B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduce (iii) ⇒ (i): continuity of positive linear functionals from decomposition property by contradiction with a sequence (x_n) violating boundedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples: determine F and (i)/(ii) (Problem 5.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: For specified spaces and cones (a) E=C([0,1]), P=nonnegative functions; (b) same with zeros at endpoints; (c) E=C^1_0 with P nonnegative functions — determine F and check whether (i) or (ii) holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator coercivity equivalences (Problem 6.A overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A:D(A)⊂E→E* be closed unbounded with ⟨Ax,x⟩ ≥ 0. Show equivalence between: (i) ∀x∈D(A) ∃C(x) s.t. ⟨Ay,y−x⟩ ≥ C(x) ∀y∈D(A); and (ii) ∃k≥0 with |⟨Ay,x⟩| ≤ k(||x|| + ||Ax||) ||Ay|| for all x,y ∈ D(A) (text gives formulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove (ii)⇒(i) directly; conversely construct bounds via convexity and exercise 2.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local uniform bound from coercivity (Problem 6.A2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming (i), prove existence of R>0, M≥0 such that ⟨Ay, x−y⟩ ≤ M for y∈D(A) and x∈D(A) with ||x||+||Ax|| ≤ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Consider function φ(x)=sup_{y∈D(A)} ⟨Ay, x−y⟩ and apply Exercise 2.1.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive quadratic estimate (Problem 6.A3–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: From previous deduce inequality |⟨Ay,x⟩|^2 ≤ 4M ⟨Ay,y⟩ for y∈D(A) and x with norm+graph-norm≤R, and conclude equivalence (i)⇔(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalences when domain is whole space (Problem 6.B1–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming D(A)=E, establish equivalences between bounds on ||Ay||, and inequalities ⟨Ay,y−x⟩ ≥ −(1/4)α^2||x||^2, relate to adjoint operator A* versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use same method as part A; deduce adjoint inequalities accordingly.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Gap metric and subspace distance properties (Problem 7.A1–3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define ρ(M,N)=sup_{||x||≤1, x∈M} dist(x,N). Show basic properties: ρ≤1, if N⊂M with N≠M then ρ=1; triangle-type bound ρ(M,L) ≤ a + b + ab for a=ρ(M,N), b=ρ(N,L); deduce consequences (if inclusions and small constants then equality). Also show ρ(M,N)=ρ(N^⊥,M^⊥).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use Lemma 6.1 and Theorem 1.12 for dual characterizations.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Gap metric for graphs of operators and adjoints (Problem 7.B1–2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given closed densely defined operators A,B, set ρ(A,B)=ρ(G(A),G(B)). Prove ρ(A,B)=ρ(B*,A*), and if D(A)∩D(B) dense then A*+B* ⊂ (A+B)* (in general inclusion may be strict).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perturbation condition (H) implies closedness and gap bound (Problem 7.B3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume D(A)⊂D(B) and ∃k∈[0,1), C≥0 s.t. ||Bu|| ≤ k||Au|| + C||u|| ∀u∈D(A). Prove A+B closed and ρ(A,A+B) ≤ k + C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoint perturbation condition and equality of adjoints (Problem 7.B4–5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume analogous condition (H') on adjoints. For small ε with ε(k+C) ≤ 1/3 and ε(k'+C') ≤1/3 prove A + εB* = A* + εB*, and under (H) and (H') deduce (A+B)* = A* + B*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: [Hint: Use successive steps and an inequality controlling Bu norm in terms of Au + tBu.]

rubrics_metrics.name: Schur's theorem setup in ℓ^1 (Problem 8 intro and 1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let E=ℓ^1 and sequence (x_n) weakly→0. Using metric d on BE*, compactness, Baire category and decomposition arguments, prove ||x_n||_1 → 0 (Schur's theorem) and related stronger convergence statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct metric d(f,g)=∑ 2^{-i}|f_i − g_i| on BE* and follow steps: define F_k, use Baire to find neighborhood, choose N, bound ||x_n||_1 by tail + finite sum, conclude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterexample in L^1 (Problem 8.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct sequence (u_n) in L^1(0,1) weakly→0 but with ||u_n||_1 =1 for all n (shows Schur fails in L^1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hahn–Banach for weak topology separation (Problem 9.A1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A,B ⊂ E* convex nonempty, A∩B=∅ and A open in σ(E*,E). Prove existence of x∈E, x≠0, and α with hyperplane {f; ⟨f,x⟩=α} separating A and B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum of closed and compact sets closed (Problem 9.A2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume A closed in σ(E*,E) and B compact in σ(E*,E). Prove A+B is closed in σ(E*,E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict separation by weak Hahn–Banach (Problem 9.A3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A closed and B compact in σ(E*,E) and A∩B=∅, prove there exists x∈E, x≠0, and α s.t. hyperplane strictly separates A and B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convexity preserved under weak closure (Problem 9.A4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A ⊂ E* convex. Prove A^{σ(E*,E)} (closure in σ(E*,E)) is convex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bipolar / double orthogonal identity in weak topology (Problem 9.B1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For linear subspace N ⊂ E*, prove N^{⊥⊥} = N^{σ(E*,E)}. What if E is reflexive? Deduce c0 dense in ℓ^∞ in σ(ℓ^∞,ℓ^1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convex l.s.c. conjugate continuity (Problem 9.B2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If ϕ : E → (−∞,+∞] convex l.s.c. (≠+∞), prove ψ = ϕ* is l.s.c. in σ(E*,E). Conversely given ψ convex l.s.c. in σ(E*,E) with ψ≠+∞ prove ∃ϕ convex l.s.c. with ψ=ϕ*.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and domain descriptions for adjoint (Problem 9.B3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For densely defined closed A:D(A)⊂E→F, prove R(A*)^{σ(E*,E)} = N(A)⊥ and D(A*)^{σ(F*,F)} = F*; discuss reflexive cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Density of J(B_E) in bidual ball (Problem 9.B4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove J(B_E) is dense in B_{E**} in topology σ(E** ,E*), without using Lemma 3.3 (see Lemma 3.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotone image contained in weak closure of convex hull (Problem 9.B5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A: B_E → E* monotone map (⟨Ax − Ay, x − y⟩ ≥ 0). Set S_E = {x; ||x||=1}. Prove A(B_E) ⊂ conv A(S_E)^{σ(E*,E)}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eberlein–Šmulian: weak compactness equivalent to sequential compactness (Problem 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show for A ⊂ E, B = closure_{σ(E,E*)} A, that (P) B σ(E,E*) compact ⇔ (Q) every sequence in A has weakly convergent subsequence. Also (P)⇒(R) property about approximating boundary points by sequences from A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof split into parts: show (P)⇒(Q) for separable case then general, use metricization argument and Lemma in part B to construct approximating sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banach–Dieudonné–Krein–Šmulian criterion for weak closedness (Problem 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let C ⊂ E* convex and assume for each n the set C ∩ nB_{E*} is σ(E*,E)-closed. Prove C is σ(E*,E)-closed. Steps involve constructing sequence (x_n) with ||x_n||→0 but sup_n ⟨f,x_n⟩ >1 for all f∈C, then deducing contradiction to get a separating x with ⟨f,x⟩≥1 ∀f∈C, and conclude.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Hahn–Banach for weak topology and sequence/finite subset constructions provided in the problem parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convex conjugation and domain equality for inf-convolution in reflexive spaces (Problem 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let E reflexive and ϕ,ψ convex l.s.c. with D(ϕ)∩D(ψ)≠∅. Set θ = ϕ* ∇ ψ*. Show D((ϕ+ψ)*) = D(ϕ*) + D(ψ*), and under extra (H) conditions establish (ϕ+ψ)* = ϕ* ∇ ψ*, domain identity, and duality inf-sup equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parts A and B elaborate boundedness of certain level sets, lower semicontinuity of θ, and Fenchel duality. Use Corollary 2.5 and previous exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of duality map and uniform convexity (Problem 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming E* strictly convex so duality map F(x) single-valued, prove Gateaux derivative limit identity, continuity statements of F (strong→weak), algebraic identities for F(x)+F(y), deduce bijectivity when E reflexive and strictly convex, and, when E* uniformly convex, prove F is uniformly continuous on bounded sets and norm differentiability results; conversely deduce uniform convexity of E* from properties of F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hints referencing Exercise 1.25 and inequalities indicated in the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regularization of convex functions by inf-convolution (Problem 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume E* uniformly convex and ϕ convex l.s.c. ≠+∞. For each x define φ_x(f)=1/2||f||^2 + ϕ*(f) − ⟨f,x⟩ and show unique minimizer f_x exists and map x→S_x is continuous. Define ψ(x)=inf_y { 1/2||x−y||^2 + ϕ(y) } and show ψ convex, differentiable with differential S_x, and construct ϕ_n via inf-convolution which are convex, differentiable and increase to ϕ pointwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Fenchel duality and Theorem 1.12; see Exercise 1.24 for method.
